hooks.text: Saturn has an icy moon shaped like a sponge.
One of Saturn's moons is forty percent empty space.
Meteor strikes on Saturn's strangest moon blast zero debris.

title: The Saturnian Moon That Acts Like a Sponge
description: Hyperion is a bizarre moon that is roughly forty percent empty space. This causes meteor impacts to compress its surface like foam rather than blasting out debris.

beats.text: Saturn has an icy moon shaped like a sponge.
beats.visual: Cassini false-color image of Saturn moon Hyperion showing sponge texture, 2005

beats.text: When Cassini arrived in 2005, its craters looked wrong.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the Cassini spacecraft during its flyby of Saturn, 2005

beats.text: Normal impacts blast debris everywhere, but this moon has almost none.
beats.visual: Cassini close-up view of heavily cratered sponge terrain on Hyperion, 2005

beats.text: The secret: roughly forty percent of Hyperion is empty space.
beats.visual: Cassini full-disk image showing irregular shape and porous surface of Hyperion, 2005

beats.text: Because it's porous ice, meteors don't blast debris outward.
beats.visual: Cassini close-up of Helios crater on Hyperion with deep honeycomb walls, 2005

beats.text: They punch directly inward, compressing the ice like foam.
beats.visual: Illustration showing impact compression of porous ice compared to rock excavation, 2007

beats.text: Gravity from giant Titan also forces the moon into a chaotic tumble.
beats.visual: Cassini photo of Saturn with its giant moon Titan in the foreground, 2005

beats.text: Its axis wobbles in a spin that's completely unpredictable.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating chaotic rotation and tumbling axis of moon Hyperion, 1989

beats.text: That unpredictable spin is unique to this giant cosmic sponge.
beats.visual: Cassini high-resolution false color disk view of Hyperion, 2005

better_than_last: Applied the reviewer's specific wording for the chaotic tumble and spin while maintaining a sub-95-word count and a clean syntactical loop back to the sponge hook.
